the Americas|1992 Portland]]|[[1992 United States men's Olympic basketball team|Men's basketball]]}} }} '''John Houston Stockton''' (born March 26, 1962) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Regarded as one of the greatest [[point guard]]s of all time, he [[List of NBA players who have spent their entire career with one franchise|spent his entire NBA career]] (1984–2003) with the [[Utah Jazz]]. The team made the playoffs in each of his 19 seasons. In [[1997 NBA Finals|1997]] and again in [[1998 NBA Finals|1998]], Stockton and his longtime teammate [[Karl Malone]] led the Jazz to the [[NBA Finals]]; each time, the team was defeated in six games by the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Stockton was a ten-time [[NBA All-Star]] and holds the NBA records for most career [[assist (basketball)|assists]] and [[steal (basketball)|steals]] by wide margins. He was inducted into the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]] in 2009 as an individual, and again in 2010 as a member of the [[1992 United States men's Olympic basketball team|1992 United States Olympic basketball team]]. In 1996, he was named one of the [[50 Greatest Players in NBA History|50 greatest players in NBA history]]. In October 2021, Stockton was again honored as one of the league's greatest players of all time by being named to the [[NBA 75th Anniversary Team]].

'''John Edwards''' (born July 31, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He played the [[center (basketball)|center]] position.

Edwards played collegiately for [[Kent State University]].  While at Kent State, Edwards was part of two of the [[Kent State Golden Flashes men's basketball|Golden Flashes]] trips to the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA tournament]] which included their appearance in the 2002 [[Elite Eight]]. He was named [[Mid-American Conference]] Defensive Player of the Year and a first-team all-conference pick in his final season and holds the Kent State record for season and career [[block (basketball)|blocked shots]].<ref name="NBA bio">{{cite web|title=John Edwards |url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/john_edwards/bio.html |publisher=NBA |accessdate=April 1, 2012 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100321195446/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/john_edwards/bio.html |archivedate=March 21, 2010 }}</ref>

He was invited to the [[Indiana Pacers]] training camp in 2004. Mainly due to his size, and some unexpected injuries to the Pacers big men early in the season, he was the only [[free agent]] training camp invitee to earn a spot on the main roster. Even so, he was expected to be released as soon as the Pacers got healthy, but the rash of suspensions resulting from the [[Pacers–Pistons brawl|November 19, 2004, brawl]] at [[The Palace of Auburn Hills]] enabled him to remain on the team. As a result of this and other injuries to the bench, the Pacers were only able to dress six players and Edwards constituted the team's entire bench.

During the summer of 2005, Edwards signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]], and, during the [[2005–06 NBA season]], he averaged 8.6 minutes per game.

On August 22, 2006, Edwards was traded back to the Pacers, along with [[Al Harrington]], in exchange for a [[2007 NBA draft|2007 first-round draft]] pick.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=2557921 |title=Pacers get Harrington from Hawks for first-round pick|date=August 22, 2006 }}</ref> He was waived in preseason, and split time with two [[NBDL]] teams in 2006–07. Edwards signed with the [[Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] in December 2006<ref>{{cite web |url=http://cache.nba.com/dleague/albuquerque/edwards_061209.html |title=Albuquerque Acquires John Edwards |publisher=NBA Development League, LLC |date=December 9, 2006 |accessdate=February 26, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140305130910/http://cache.nba.com/dleague/albuquerque/edwards_061209.html |archivedate=March 5, 2014  }}</ref> then with the [[Tulsa 66ers]] the following month.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/roster_moves_070131.html |title=Jam, Skyforce, 66ers Make Roster Moves |website=[[NBA.com]] |date=January 31, 2007 |accessdate=February 26, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309115652/http://www.nba.com/dleague/roster_moves_070131.html |archivedate=March 9, 2014  }}</ref> The following season, also during preseason, Edwards was waived by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], signing in November 2007 with [[Cherkassy (basketball)|Cherkassy]].

Edwards returned to the D-League when he signed with the [[Iowa Energy]] in March 2009.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/usa/nbdl/1141/energy_sign_john_edwards_.html |title=Energy Sign John Edwards |date=March 27, 2009 |accessdate=February 26, 2014}}</ref> The Energy traded Edwards to the [[Bakersfield Jam]] in January 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/jam_adds_size_trade_with_iowa_2010_01_19.html |title=Jam Adds Size in Trade With Iowa |website=[[NBA.com]] |date=January 19, 2010 |accessdate=February 26, 2014 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309115649/http://www.nba.com/dleague/bakersfield/jam_adds_size_trade_with_iowa_2010_01_19.html |archivedate=March 9, 2014  }}</ref>

He played in the 2010–2011 season with the [[A1 Ethniki|Greek League]] team [[Colossus Rhodes BC|Colossus Rhodes]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.galanissportsdata.com/basketball/mena1/Season2009_10/a1teamrs.asp?t=08 |publisher=Galanissportsdata.com |title=KOLOSSOS VAP (Total Stats Regular Season After day ) |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100307053656/http://www.galanissportsdata.com/basketball/mena1/Season2009_10/a1teamrs.asp?t=08 |archivedate=March 7, 2010  }}</ref> He then played in Puerto Rico, before moving to Poland to play for [[Turów Zgorzelec]]. In 2012, he signed with [[BC Tsmoki-Minsk]] in Belarus.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=BLR&PlayerID=36188 |title=John Edwards |publisher=Eurobasket}}</ref>  He retired from basketball in 2013 and is pursuing a career in Information Technology.

'''John Thomas''' (born September 8, 1975) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. He was the captain of the [[1996–97 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|1996–97 Minnesota Golden Gophers]] team that advanced to the [[1997 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Final Four – Indianapolis, Indiana|1997 NCAA Semi-Final]].

Thomas was selected by the [[New York Knicks]] with the 25th pick in the [[1997 NBA draft]], although he never played a game with them as he was traded, along with [[Dontae' Jones]], [[Walter McCarty]] and [[Scott Brooks]], to the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Chris Mills (basketball)|Chris Mills]] and two conditional second-round draft choices on October 22, 1997. Four months later, he was again traded, this time to the [[Toronto Raptors]], alongside [[Chauncey Billups]], [[Dee Brown (basketball, born 1968)|Dee Brown]] and [[Roy Rogers (basketball)|Roy Rogers]], for [[Kenny Anderson (basketball)|Kenny Anderson]], [[Zan Tabak]] and [[Popeye Jones]]. Jerebko played a total of 10 seasons in the NBA with four different teams, the [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Utah Jazz]] and [[Golden State Warriors]].
